entities.name: Malaria
entities.description: Life-threatening protozoan intraerythrocytic parasitic infection caused by Plasmodium species, characterized by cyclical fever paroxysms, acute hemolysis, profound thrombocytopenia, and risk of microvascular sequestration or multiorgan failure.

entities.name: Nocturnal Anopheles Mosquito Bite
entities.description: Primary vector transmission via the bite of infective nocturnal female mosquitoes of the genus Anopheles (e.g., An. gambiae, An. funestus, An. stephensi), typically feeding between dusk and dawn.

entities.name: Tropical Endemic Area Travel or Residence
entities.description: Recent travel to or residence in malaria-endemic tropical and subtropical regions, predominantly sub-Saharan Africa (>95% global burden), South and Southeast Asia, Western Pacific, and the Amazon basin.

entities.name: Infected Blood Transfusion or Contaminated Needle Sharing
entities.description: Non-vector parenteral transmission occurring through blood product transfusions, needle sharing among intravenous drug users, or vertical congenital transmission from mother to fetus.

entities.name: Plasmodium falciparum
entities.description: Deadliest human malaria protozoan; invades erythrocytes of all ages, induces high-density parasitemia, PfEMP1-mediated endothelial cytoadherence, microvascular sequestration, and severe multi-organ dysfunction.

entities.name: Plasmodium vivax
entities.description: Most widespread human malaria parasite outside Africa; selectively infects reticulocytes, forms dormant hepatic hypnozoites capable of periodic clinical relapses months to years post-inoculation.

entities.name: Plasmodium ovale
entities.description: Benign tertian malaria protozoan primarily endemic in sub-Saharan West and Central Africa; selectively invades reticulocytes and forms persistent intrahepatic hypnozoites causing delayed relapses.

entities.name: Plasmodium malariae
entities.description: Human malaria species characterized by a 72-hour quartan erythrocytic replication cycle, selectivity for senescent erythrocytes, low parasitemia, and potential to cause chronic immune-complex nephrotic syndrome.

entities.name: Plasmodium knowlesi
entities.description: Zoonotic simian malaria parasite endemic in Southeast Asia (macaque reservoir) with an ultra-rapid 24-hour replication cycle causing daily quotidian fevers and rapid progression to severe malaria.

entities.name: Classical Malarial Paroxysm with Rigors and Diaphoresis
entities.description: Pathognomonic triphasic fever attack synchronous with erythrocyte schizont rupture: sudden cold stage with violent shivering and rigors (15-60 min), hot stage with fever spike to 39-41°C (2-6 hr), and drenching sweating defervescence stage (2-4 hr).

entities.name: Periodic Tertian or Quartan Fever Rhythm
entities.description: Synchronous recurring fever spike patterns: tertian rhythm every 48 hours in P. vivax/ovale/falciparum, quartan rhythm every 72 hours in P. malariae, or quotidian rhythm every 24 hours in P. knowlesi.

entities.name: Tender Splenomegaly with Hemolytic Jaundice and Pallor
entities.description: Clinical triad consisting of an acutely enlarged, soft, tender spleen appearing within 3-7 days, accompanied by mild scleral icterus and conjunctival/mucocutaneous pallor.

entities.name: Cerebral Malaria with Impaired Consciousness and Convulsions
entities.description: Cardinal manifestation of severe P. falciparum malaria characterized by coma (Glasgow Coma Scale < 11 in adults or Blantyre Coma Score < 3 in children), generalized seizures, and malarial retinopathy.

entities.name: Blackwater Fever with Hemoglobinuria and Acute Renal Failure
entities.description: Severe clinical hallmark featuring dark mahogany or black-colored urine resulting from massive intravascular hemolysis and hemoglobinuria, associated with oliguria and rapid creatinine elevation.

entities.name: Severe Lactic Acidosis with Kussmaul Breathing
entities.description: Deep, rapid, labored hyperventilation (Kussmaul breathing) in severe malaria driven by marked systemic lactic acidosis (> 5 mmol/L) and microvascular capillary hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Intraerythrocytic Parasites on Giemsa Blood Smear
entities.description: Definitive admission microscopy on thick and thin blood films showing intraerythrocytic ring-form trophozoites, crescentic banana-shaped gametocytes (P. falciparum), or amoeboid forms with Schüffner dots (P. vivax).

entities.name: Positive Malaria Rapid Diagnostic Test for HRP2 and pLDH
entities.description: Rapid immunochromatographic antigen detection on fingerstick blood positive for Plasmodium falciparum Histidine-Rich Protein 2 (HRP2) and/or pan-Plasmodium parasite lactate dehydrogenase (pLDH) or aldolase.

entities.name: Hemolytic Anemia with Depleted Haptoglobin and Elevated LDH
entities.description: Normocytic normochromic anemia with acute hemoglobin/hematocrit drop, undetectable serum haptoglobin (< 0.1 g/L), marked serum lactate dehydrogenase elevation (LDH > 500-1000 IU/L), and elevated reticulocyte count.

entities.name: Profound Thrombocytopenia with Normal or Low WBC Count
entities.description: Platelet count markedly depressed (< 100,000/µL, frequently < 50,000/µL) in 70-85% of patients, accompanied by a normal or leukopenic white blood cell count (3,000-6,000/µL) without marked bacterial leukocytosis.

entities.name: Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia with Mild Transaminitis
entities.description: Elevation of indirect (unconjugated) serum bilirubin (> 2-3 mg/dL) with normal or only modestly elevated transaminases (AST and ALT < 3x upper limit of normal), confirming hemolytic rather than obstructive or hepatocellular jaundice.

entities.name: POCUS Splenomegaly with Normal Gallbladder Wall
entities.description: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) demonstrating homogenous splenomegaly and mild hepatomegaly with thin, non-edematous gallbladder wall (< 3 mm) and absence of subcapsular splenic hematoma, abscess, or plasma leakage.

entities.name: Symptom Onset Less Than 7 Days Post-Exposure
entities.description: Presentation with fever and constitutional symptoms within less than 7 days after first exposure or arrival in a malaria-endemic region.

entities.name: Three Consecutive Negative Quality-Assured Blood Smears and RDTs
entities.description: Three consecutive high-magnification thick and thin blood Giemsa smears and antigen-based RDTs performed 12 to 24 hours apart yielding negative parasite results.

entities.name: Marked Microvascular Plasma Leakage with Hemoconcentration
entities.description: Presence of systemic plasma leakage evidenced by hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise >= 20%), pleural effusion, ascites, or stratified gallbladder wall edema on imaging.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis Exceeding 15000 per Microliter
entities.description: Prominent neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC > 15,000/µL) with significant left shift and toxic granulation on admission CBC.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Acute viral arboviral infection caused by Dengue virus transmitted by Aedes aegypti, presenting with saddleback fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgia, hemoconcentration, and plasma leakage.

entities.name: Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Invasive systemic salmonellosis caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi presenting with prolonged step-ladder fever, relative bradycardia, rose spots, and abdominal symptoms.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal illness caused by Leptospira interrogans transmitted via floodwater or rodent urine, presenting with biphasic fever, conjunctival suffusion, calf tenderness, jaundice, and acute renal failure.

entities.name: Scrub Typhus
entities.description: Zoonotic mite-borne infection caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi transmitted by larval trombiculid chiggers, presenting with acute fever, regional lymphadenopathy, maculopapular rash, and eschar.

entities.name: Rapid Defervescence Following Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy
entities.description: Dramatic clinical defervescence to normal body temperature and >90% reduction in circulating asexual parasites within 24 to 48 hours of starting oral Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT).

entities.name: Intravenous Artesunate Parasite Clearance in Severe Malaria
entities.description: Rapid destruction of circulating and sequestered ring-stage Plasmodium parasites following parenteral intravenous artesunate (2.4 mg/kg IV), significantly reducing mortality in severe complicated malaria.

entities.name: Hypnozoite Eradication by 8-Aminoquinolines
entities.description: Radical cure of dormant liver-stage hypnozoites in Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale infections using a 14-day course of Primaquine or single-dose Tafenoquine following confirmation of normal G6PD activity.

entities.name: Intrinsic Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial Agents
entities.description: Total lack of defervescence, persistent fever paroxysms, and ongoing intraerythrocytic parasitemia when empirically treated with standard broad-spectrum antibacterial agents (beta-lactams, cephalosporins, aminoglycosides).

relationships.target: Nocturnal Anopheles Mosquito Bite
relationships.keywords: TRANSMITTED_BY, mosquito vector, anopheles, nocturnal feeding
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Malaria is primarily transmitted through the nocturnal bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes inoculating sporozoites during blood meals taken between dusk and dawn.

relationships.target: Tropical Endemic Area Travel or Residence
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, geographic endemicity, travel history, tropical medicine
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Exposure occurs through living in or travelling to tropical and subtropical transmission zones, where sub-Saharan Africa carries over 95% of worldwide cases and fatalities.

relationships.target: Infected Blood Transfusion or Contaminated Needle Sharing
relationships.keywords: TRANSMITTED_BY, parenteral inoculation, blood transfusion, congenital transmission
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Malaria can be transmitted parenterally without mosquito vectors via transfusion of infected erythrocytic units, contaminated needle sharing, or vertically across the placenta.

relationships.target: Plasmodium falciparum
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, causative agent, malignant tertian, cytoadherence
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Plasmodium falciparum causes malignant tertian malaria and is responsible for >95% of malaria deaths worldwide, driven by universal erythrocyte invasion, extensive cytoadherence, and deep capillary sequestration.

relationships.target: Plasmodium vivax
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, causative agent, benign tertian, hypnozoites, relapsing malaria
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Plasmodium vivax produces benign tertian malaria with reticulocyte tropism and dormant liver-stage hypnozoites that cause recurrent relapses at periodic intervals if radical cure is not achieved.

relationships.target: Plasmodium ovale
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, causative agent, ovale tertian, dormant hypnozoites
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Plasmodium ovale produces tertian fever paroxysms and harbours latent hypnozoites in hepatocytes leading to late clinical relapses.

relationships.target: Plasmodium malariae
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, causative agent, quartan malaria, chronic infection, nephrotic syndrome
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Plasmodium malariae induces quartan fever periodicities every 72 hours, restricted to aging erythrocytes, and can persist asymptomatically for decades or provoke chronic glomerulonephritis.

relationships.target: Plasmodium knowlesi
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, causative agent, zoonotic malaria, quotidian fever, 24-hour cycle
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Plasmodium knowlesi is a zoonotic parasite transmitted from wild macaque hosts in Southeast Asia that replicates every 24 hours, often generating hyperparasitemia and rapid clinical collapse.

relationships.target: Classical Malarial Paroxysm with Rigors and Diaphoresis
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, malarial paroxysm, rigors, diaphoresis, rules in
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The classical malarial paroxysm corresponds to synchronous intravascular schizont rupture, sequentially progressing through violent teeth-chattering rigors, intense hyperpyrexia with throbbing cephalalgia, and drenching diaphoresis with rapid defervescence.

relationships.target: Periodic Tertian or Quartan Fever Rhythm
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, fever periodicity, tertian rhythm, quartan fever
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Regular fever periodicity recurring every 48 hours (tertian) or every 72 hours (quartan) matches the synchronized merozoite release cycle and strongly differentiates malaria from continuous bacterial fevers.

relationships.target: Tender Splenomegaly with Hemolytic Jaundice and Pallor
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, splenomegaly, hemolytic icterus, anemia pallor
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Early palpable, tender splenomegaly combined with scleral icterus and mucosal pallor is a hallmark physical examination triad reflecting acute splenic sequestration and active erythrocyte hemolysis.

relationships.target: Cerebral Malaria with Impaired Consciousness and Convulsions
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, cerebral malaria, coma, convulsions, malarial retinopathy
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Cerebral malaria manifests at admission as unarousable coma, recurrent generalized convulsions, and characteristic retinal whitening/hemorrhages driven by sequestered parasitized erythrocytes in cerebral capillaries.

relationships.target: Blackwater Fever with Hemoglobinuria and Acute Renal Failure
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, blackwater fever, hemoglobinuria, acute tubular necrosis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Blackwater fever is a dramatic presentation of massive intravascular hemolysis yielding port-wine to black urine from severe hemoglobinuria, culminating in acute tubular necrosis and renal compromise.

relationships.target: Severe Lactic Acidosis with Kussmaul Breathing
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, metabolic acidosis, Kussmaul respiration, respiratory distress
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Deep labored respiratory distress (acidotic Kussmaul breathing) represents systemic tissue hypoxia and lactic acidosis (lactate > 5 mmol/L), serving as one of the strongest bedside predictors of mortality.

relationships.target: Intraerythrocytic Parasites on Giemsa Blood Smear
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, blood smear microscopy, Giemsa stain, ring trophozoites, parasitemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Peripheral blood Giemsa stain microscopy at triage provides definitive confirmation, with thick smears detecting low-level parasitemia and thin smears quantifying percentage parasitemia and differentiating Plasmodium species.

relationships.target: Positive Malaria Rapid Diagnostic Test for HRP2 and pLDH
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, rapid diagnostic test, RDT, HRP2, pLDH antigen
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside RDTs rapidly detect circulating HRP2 and pLDH antigens at admission triage, confirming active or recent falciparum and non-falciparum Plasmodium parasitemia within 15 minutes.

relationships.target: Hemolytic Anemia with Depleted Haptoglobin and Elevated LDH
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, hemolytic anemia, depleted haptoglobin, elevated LDH, reticulocytosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission laboratory profile exhibits brisk intravascular and extravascular hemolysis characterized by an acute drop in hemoglobin, undetectable haptoglobin, markedly elevated serum LDH, and compensatory reticulocytosis.

relationships.target: Profound Thrombocytopenia with Normal or Low WBC Count
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, splenic pooling, admission CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Complete blood count at triage characteristically shows profound thrombocytopenia (< 100,000/µL) alongside a normal or low leukocyte count (3,000-6,000/µL) resulting from splenic pooling and immune platelet destruction.

relationships.target: Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia with Mild Transaminitis
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, unconjugated jaundice, mild transaminitis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hepatic chemistry at admission demonstrates predominant unconjugated (indirect) hyperbilirubinemia with minimal transaminase elevation (< 3x ULN), reflecting extensive erythrocyte destruction rather than viral hepatitis.

relationships.target: POCUS Splenomegaly with Normal Gallbladder Wall
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, POCUS ultrasound, splenomegaly, normal gallbladder, no plasma leakage
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside POCUS reveals acute splenomegaly with a normal thin gallbladder wall and absence of third-space plasma leakage, distinguishing malaria from the acute thickened edematous gallbladder wall seen in dengue.

relationships.target: Symptom Onset Less Than 7 Days Post-Exposure
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, incubation period
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Symptom onset occurring less than 7 days after initial entry into an endemic zone rules out Plasmodium falciparum malaria, because hepatic intrahepatic schizogony requires an obligatory biological minimum incubation of 7 to 9 days.

relationships.target: Three Consecutive Negative Quality-Assured Blood Smears and RDTs
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, serial microscopy, negative RDT
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Three consecutive quality-assured thick and thin Giemsa smears alongside negative antigen RDTs obtained 12 to 24 hours apart completely rules out acute symptomatic malaria as the etiology of the current febrile illness.

relationships.target: Marked Microvascular Plasma Leakage with Hemoconcentration
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, plasma leakage, hemoconcentration
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of significant microvascular plasma leakage with hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise >= 20%), pleural effusion, or ascites rules out uncomplicated malaria, pointing decisively toward severe dengue shock syndrome.

relationships.target: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis Exceeding 15000 per Microliter
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, leukocytosis, bacterial sepsis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC > 15,000/µL) strongly excludes uncomplicated malaria, which typically presents with normal or leukopenic white counts (3,000-6,000/µL); high leukocytosis indicates pyogenic bacterial sepsis, leptospirosis, or enteric perforation.

relationships.target: Dengue Fever
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, arbovirus, hemoconcentration
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Dengue Fever is differentiated at triage by severe retro-orbital headache, positive tourniquet test, hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise >= 20%), plasma leakage (pleural effusion, gallbladder wall edema), and AST > ALT elevation without splenomegaly or hemolytic jaundice; in contrast, Malaria features hemolytic anemia with low hematocrit, unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, early splenomegaly, and intraerythrocytic parasites on blood smear.

relationships.target: Typhoid Fever
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, enteric fever, Faget sign
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Typhoid Fever is differentiated by an insidious step-ladder gradual temperature rise, relative bradycardia (Faget sign), rose spots on the trunk, dull apathetic facies, and lack of cyclical sweating rigors; in contrast, Malaria presents with sudden-onset violent teeth-chattering rigors, drenching diaphoresis, acute hemolytic anemia, and rapid defervescence cycles.

relationships.target: Leptospirosis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, spirochete, conjunctival suffusion
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis is differentiated by striking bilateral conjunctival suffusion without purulent exudate, severe gastrocnemius calf tenderness, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC > 15,000/µL), and direct (conjugated) hyperbilirubinemia with elevated ESR/CRP; in contrast, Malaria presents with unconjugated (indirect) hyperbilirubinemia, normal/low WBC, and Giemsa smear parasite visualization.

relationships.target: Scrub Typhus
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, rickettsia, eschar
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scrub Typhus is differentiated by a pathognomonic necrotic cigarette-burn eschar at the chigger bite site, regional lymphadenopathy, and generalized macular trunk rash; in contrast, Malaria lacks eschars and rash, and is diagnosed by intraerythrocytic ring forms and positive HRP2/pLDH antigen tests.

relationships.target: Rapid Defervescence Following Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, therapeutic verification, artemisinin response, defervescence, ACT
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Uncomplicated malaria responds rapidly to oral Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (e.g., artemether-lumefantrine, artesunate-amodiaquine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) with complete fever resolution and profound (>90%) asexual parasite clearance within 24 to 48 hours.

relationships.target: Intravenous Artesunate Parasite Clearance in Severe Malaria
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, therapeutic verification, severe malaria, intravenous artesunate, rapid parasite clearance
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Severe complicated malaria responds swiftly to parenteral intravenous artesunate administered at 0, 12, and 24 hours, clearing circulating ring-stage parasitemia faster than intravenous quinine and lowering overall clinical mortality.

relationships.target: Hypnozoite Eradication by 8-Aminoquinolines
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, therapeutic verification, radical cure, primaquine, tafenoquine, hypnozoites
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Relapsing malaria caused by P. vivax and P. ovale responds to radical cure with 8-aminoquinolines (Primaquine or Tafenoquine), which eradicate dormant intrahepatic hypnozoites and abolish long-latency recurrent relapses once G6PD deficiency is excluded.

relationships.target: Intrinsic Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial Agents
relationships.keywords: INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO, antibiotic failure, intrinsic resistance, lack of defervescence
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Plasmodium species are intrinsically unresponsive to standard empirical broad-spectrum antibacterials (penicillins, 3rd-generation cephalosporins, aminoglycosides), resulting in continued fever paroxysms and unabated parasite proliferation.
